title: Record S13's review round 1
message:
Record S13's review round 1

Nine findings on MR !20, each with its fix commit, what was decided
differently from the proposal or from the plan, the two work items filed
on the way, and the verification.

title: Describe the review fixes in the system documents
message:
Describe the review fixes in the system documents

The database document gains the deadlock mark, what a site does when a
COMMIT's outcome cannot be read back, and the pool query's cleared
result. The save-systems document gains the single player-save writer,
the second write of a leaving save, the flags an incomplete save sets,
a sheath in a house, and the pet keeper's wait for an unreadable row.
The vessel document gains the event's idempotent finish and the plunder
bounty that is announced only when recorded. The testing guide gains the
two test techniques the fixes needed.

title: Announce a plunder's bounty only when it was recorded
message:
Announce a plunder's bounty only when it was recorded

S13 stopped vessel_bounty_record_offense() from overwriting a bounty it
could not read; the offense is dropped instead. vessel_add_bounty() could
not report that, so do_plunder told the player the bounty rose and
passed the amount on as already applied, and nothing applied it later.

vessel_add_bounty() now returns whether the offense was recorded and
tries once more first: outside a transaction, a connection that failed
one statement has reconnected by then. do_plunder announces the bounty
and passes it on only when it was recorded; otherwise the staff are told
the amount to apply by hand.

MR !20 review, P3.

title: Keep hedit from saving over an entry it did not load
message:
Keep hedit from saving over an entry it did not load

Since S13 the save deletes the stored keywords that are not in the
editor's list. That is right only for the entry the editor loaded. Two
paths save under another entry's tag: "hedit <word>" offers a new entry
when no keyword starts with the word, though an entry's tag may equal
it, and menu option 1 retags the open entry. The save then overwrote the
other entry's text, as before, and now deleted its keywords, which are
archived nowhere.

The editor keeps the tag of the entry it loaded (none for a new entry)
in its storage field once the menu is open. Inside its transaction, a
save under any other tag locks that tag's row and is refused when the
row exists; the editor stays open for another tag.

MR !20 review, P3.

title: Clear the pool query's result before it can fail
message:
Clear the pool query's result before it can fail

mysql_pool_query() wrote *result only when the query succeeded.
log_hint_usage() passes an uninitialized pointer, ignores the return
value and frees the pointer when it is not NULL, so any failed insert
into hint_usage_log freed stack garbage. S13 added two ways to fail: the
pool returns no connection while the database is away, and a marked
connection refuses the statement. The function now clears *result first,
which covers every caller.

The defect predates S13 (MR !20 review, P3).

title: Flag a player or house whose save was incomplete
message:
Flag a player or house whose save was incomplete

An incomplete save left PLR_CRASH or ROOM_HOUSE_CRASH as it found it.
Several callers save with the flag clear: the "save" command, the
crafting saves and the direct house saves. There the delete and the
other rows were committed, the refused object's old row was gone, and
the save passes skipped the unflagged player or room, so a crash before
the next inventory change lost the object.

Crash_crashsave() and House_crashsave() now set the flag after a save
that failed or left an object out. The house save looks its room up
before it opens the transaction instead of after the delete. The tests
no longer set the flag by hand before the save under test.

MR !20 review, P3.

title: Choose no state when a COMMIT's outcome cannot be read
message:
Choose no state when a COMMIT's outcome cannot be read

A COMMIT's reply is mostly lost to a server restart, and then the one
read-back that follows cannot connect either. The vessel event and the
pet keeper took that for a rollback.

The vessel event told the staff to retry VEVENT END, and the retry added
every leaderboard score a second time; the recovery mark it wrote first
would have erased a committed "completed". The finish is now idempotent
on the event's own row: the status is written first, only while the
event has not ended, and the scores only when that changed a row. The
recovery mark has the same condition.

The pet keeper kept a stabled pet in play beside its stored row, or
discarded a reclaimed one whose row was active, which the next pet save
deletes with its gear. With the row unreadable it now chooses neither:
the roster goes back to "restore failed", which keeps every pet row and
closes the keeper, and 'pets restore' settles it from the rows. That
restore publishes a pet whose row is active, as before, and now takes a
follower out of play whose row says the keeper has it.

MR !20 review, P2.

title: Mark a deadlock victim's transaction as lost
message:
Mark a deadlock victim's transaction as lost

On error 1213 the server rolls back the victim's whole transaction, not
the one statement, and leaves the connection up. The error packet carries
no status flags, so the library went on holding the transaction open and
the connection was not marked: the statements after the victim ran one by
one in autocommit and COMMIT reported success over nothing, the failure
S13 removes for a lost connection. The writers go on after a failed row
by design, so an object, house or cargo save would have kept the old rows
beside the ones written after the victim.

transaction_watch_end() marks the connection on ER_LOCK_DEADLOCK as well.
It takes a second session locking the same rows; the game alone cannot
deadlock with itself.

MR !20 review, P2.

title: Write a leaving character's save again before its objects go
message:
Write a leaving character's save again before its objects go

The rent, idle and cryo saves returned at a failed COMMIT, or at a failed
start, with the character's objects still in memory. Their callers go on
to extract_char(), which drops what a character holds in the room, beside
a save that holds it too: the last one, or this one when the COMMIT was
run and only its reply lost. Since S13 marks a lost transaction, every
connection lost inside one of these saves ended that way.

The four player saves now share one writer, which leaves everything in
memory. A leaving save that did not reach the database is written once
more on the session the connection has by then; the save replaces the
last one whole, so a second write is safe. The objects then leave memory
whether it was written or not, and after two failures the staff are told
that the last save stands. objsave_commit_player_save() goes into the
writer, which commits through mysql_commit_transaction().

MR !20 review, P2.

title: Write the bags in the cryo and idle saves
message:
Write the bags in the cryo and idle saves

Both saves delete the player's rows and write them again, and since S13
both commit that. The cryo save never wrote what was sorted into the
bags, and the idle save took a character with nothing worn or carried
for one with nothing to store, so with rent not free a bagged item was
gone at the next login. The cryo save writes the bags like the others,
and the idle save always writes what there is.

MR !20 review, P2.

title: Store a sheath's weapons with the house it lies in
message:
Store a sheath's weapons with the house it lies in

A house save handed its NULL owner to the sheath writer, which
dereferenced it: a sheath holding a weapon, dropped in a house, stopped
the server at the next house save. Sheath rows are stored and loaded by
their owner's name, and a house has none, so House_save() now writes the
weapons as the house's own objects, beside the sheath, and the record
writer leaves the sheath rows to saves that have an owner.

The crash predates S13 (MR !20 review, P1).

title: Record S13's build, verification and hand-off
message:
Record S13's build, verification and hand-off

The progress log, the verification on 3eab48d60 (make test-all, the boot
migration on a database built from the old definitions, the local CI
matrix, all 20 live gates and a live check with the server's database
sessions killed), and the hand-off: tag vessels-s13 and MR !20.

title: Limit a lost transaction's mark to its game pulse
message:
Limit a lost transaction's mark to its game pulse

A connection that lost its transaction refuses every statement until
the caller ends the transaction. A caller that failed without ending it
would have left the connection refusing everyone's statements until some
later save began a transaction, and the query that loads a player's
objects at login stops the server when it fails.

All 26 transaction sites end their transaction on every path, so nothing
does that today. For code written later, the mark no longer outlasts the
game pulse it was set in: all database work is done within the pulse
that starts it, so a mark met in a later pulse belongs to code that has
returned. The layer then rolls the transaction back itself, logs a
SYSERR, and lets the statement through.

title: Keep a transaction whole when its connection is lost
message:
Keep a transaction whole when its connection is lost

Every connection reconnects by itself. When one dropped inside a
transaction, the server rolled the transaction back, one command failed,
and the statements after it ran one by one on a new session, a COMMIT
among them reporting success. Work item #13.

The query layer now marks a connection that lost its transaction (a
command failed with 2006 or 2013, failed after the library gave the
transaction up, or reconnected, as a ping does) and refuses every
statement on it until the caller ends the transaction. The mark is kept
on the handle, so it survives the reconnect and goes with the handle.
mysql_commit_transaction() tells a confirmed COMMIT, a refused one and
one without a reply apart, and rolls back what is not confirmed.

Sites:
- Cargo trades use the helper; the manifest writer no longer has to stop
  at its first failure.
- Pet storage and retrieval, a hull's change of owner and the end of a
  vessel event read the database back, with a locking read, after a
  COMMIT without a reply.
- The object and sheath writers report a row that was not written. A
  save commits the rest, keeps PLR_CRASH or ROOM_HOUSE_CRASH, and tells
  the staff whose objects they were. Crash_save_single() keeps the flag
  unless the objects and the character both saved.
- An extra description that does not fit an object's record is left out
  instead of the object, in the object, sheath and pet writers.
- Crash_idlesave() commits, the empty save included. Crash_cryosave()
  takes the transaction and the delete the other saves have: it stored a
  frozen character's objects beside the last save's.
- house_data loses the unique key on vnum that let a house keep one
  object, in master_schema.sql and db_init.c, with boot migration
  2026100401 for databases made from them.
- A bounty that cannot be read is not overwritten with the new offense.
- The pool reconnects a stale handle in place instead of closing the
  handle conn points at, and returns no connection when the database is
  away instead of looping until it is back, which would have held the
  game. The two uncalled functions that closed pooled handles are gone.
- The help writers check, inside their transaction, that the session
  still holds the help synchronization lock; hedit reads the stored
  keywords from its prepared statement, so removed keywords are deleted.

Tests lose the connection for real (mysql_test_drop_connection_at()
shuts the socket down at a named statement, before it is sent or after
the server ran it and its reply was thrown away) on the real tables,
with test-only rows.

title: Plan S13: transactions that survive a lost connection
message:
Plan S13: transactions that survive a lost connection

The Phase 13 section: what the client library does on a real drop (probed),
the query-layer rule, the COMMIT helper, the four read-backs, the object
save changes, the house_data key, the site fixes, the tests, and the
planning ablation. Work item #13.

title: Leave no item unsaveable in S13
message:
Leave no item unsaveable in S13

The incomplete-save report left one case: an item whose row can never be
written is still lost at the save that ends the session. Two things can
make a row fail on a healthy database, and S13 now removes both. The
object and sheath writers refuse a record longer than their 36,767-byte
buffer; they will size the buffer for every bounded part of a record and
leave out an extra description that does not fit, the only unbounded
part, instead of the item. The fresh-install house_data definition puts
a unique key on vnum although the writer stores one row per object, so a
house created from it keeps one object; the definition loses the key,
with a migration. The live table has no such key (9,743 rows over 44
houses in the development database), and the largest of its 489,375
saved player object records is 2,400 bytes. A row that still fails is a
database fault, which the incomplete-save report covers.

title: Add the incomplete-save report to S13
message:
Add the incomplete-save report to S13

Work item #13 proposed that the object and house writers stop and fail
the save when a row cannot be written. The query-layer rule covers the
lost connection without that, but a row that fails on a good connection
is still dropped while the save reports success. S13 now has the
writers report the failed row: the save commits the rest, counts as
incomplete so the next pass retries it, and tells the staff whose item
it was. It does not fail the whole save, which would stop a player's
saves over one item that can never be written and, at rent, roll back
after worn gear has left memory.

title: Add S15 for work item #14
message:
Add S15 for work item #14

The vessel commands S11 did not reach still move gold in memory only
after writing the ship's side to the database, so a crash before the
next per-minute save keeps a purchase with its gold, or takes a sold
item or delivered freight unpaid. Work item #14 lists the fifteen gold
movements; S15 gives them S11's checked save in the passenger fare's
shape, after S14. It does not use S14's settlement record, because each
command would need its own stored undo.

title: Add S13 and S14 for work items #13 and #12
message:
Add S13 and S14 for work items #13 and #12

The two vessel work items still open join the sequence, both resolved in
this worktree. S13 (work item #13) makes "after a lost connection,
nothing but ROLLBACK" a rule of the query layer, tells an unanswered
COMMIT from a refused one at the sites that take it for a rollback, and
fixes the sites the rule does not reach. S14 (work item #12) makes cargo
trades, freight acceptance and dock-fee payment two-phase settlements,
with a settlement row and a player-file marker. S13 is next, on
feat/vessels-s13 from master ec8f55b26 (tag vessels-s13-base); S14
follows from its merge and uses its COMMIT helper. Each step's merge
request closes its work item.

Planning ablation: one step per work item. The query-layer rule replaces
the per-writer changes #13 proposed, so the object, house, pet-gear and
help writers keep their return values. Freight delivery and the vessel
purchase commands also pay in memory, but neither item names them, so
they get no step.
